q: Shannon's 1949 counting argument shows that most Boolean functions require circuit size:
exp: There are 2^{2ⁿ} Boolean functions on n bits but only (2s)^{2s} circuits of size s. Setting s = c·2ⁿ/n makes the circuit count less than the function count, so most functions require size Ω(2ⁿ/n). This non-constructive argument does not name a specific hard function.
